open_points.subject: A15 rule 6 repair view (latest NodeExecutions for a slot)
open_points.text: "surface, which may know every module, assembles every read ... and the repair view of one slot (A15 rule 6, K-12)" and "runs ... Owns A12–A15 ... and the trace"
open_points.question: Which module is the owner of the A15 rule 6 repair-view rule (filtering to function nodes pinned to any contract version of the slot, reverse store order, and page limit): `runs` or `surface`?
options: `runs` owns the repair-view selection rule and exposes a dedicated read capability that `surface` only forwards/masks
`surface` owns repair-view assembly/query logic (using module reads + `store.page_records`), while `runs` owns only run progression and trace writing
open_points.default_guess: `surface` owns repair-view assembly, because State 3 explicitly lists that read under `surface` ownership.

open_points.subject: Inspection/read boundary between owner modules and direct store paging
open_points.text: "A module reads what a module it may know owns through that module's capability, and never decides from another module's raw records ... `surface` ... assembles ... from the owning modules' read capabilities and `store.page_records`. It reads raw records only to return them"
open_points.question: For inspect/read operations, which record types may `surface` fetch directly from `store.page_records` versus only through each owning module’s read capability?
options: All inspect/read access goes through owner-module read capabilities; `store.page_records` is internal helper those modules use
`surface` may directly page raw immutable records, but must use owner-module capabilities for computed/current views
open_points.default_guess: `surface` directly pages raw records and uses owner-module capabilities only for computed values.

open_points.subject: Pre-send instance checks ownership (`bindings.check_binding_current` vs `service_invoker.prepare_request`)
open_points.text: "`bindings.check_binding_current`, which returns the current ManifestOperation M10 — ... and the `api_base_url`, `required_headers` and class of the instance ... — or `binding_stale`; then `service_invoker.prepare_request` ... checks the instance"
open_points.question: Who owns failures about selected-instance validity at send time (missing instance, missing `api_base_url`, duplicate required header names, disallowed plain HTTP): `bindings` as part of `check_binding_current`, or `service_invoker` during `prepare_request`?
options: `bindings` validates/derives instance fields and can fail before `prepare_request`
`service_invoker` performs instance validity checks; `bindings` only validates manifest entry staleness/invocability
Split: `bindings` checks manifest-entry facts only; `service_invoker` checks installation instance and transport-policy facts
open_points.default_guess: Split with `service_invoker` owning instance/transport checks (per A09 rule 6), and `bindings` owning manifest-entry staleness checks.
